title: Pilot Matter environment
description: A world built in Pilot Matter's interactive builder: the environment it was built on, that environment's own elements as they were kept, and the placements committed over them. Read by js/environment-file.js, which refuses a file this schema refuses and clamps every range a file sets to the bounds its element declares.

$schema.description: Where this schema is, for an editor that reads one.

format.description: What the file is, so a JSON file that is something else is refused by name.

version.description: The version of the format the file was written in.

name.description: The world's name, as the builder and the settings list show it.

base.description: The environment the world was built on: one of the builder's canvases.

elements.description: The environment's own elements, as they were kept - their ranges as the pilot left them.

placements.description: What was built over the environment, in the order it was committed.

start.description: Where a flight on this world begins: over the point, on the heading, at the height above the ground there. Left out, a flight opens where every world's does.

heading.description: A compass heading in degrees, read round the compass to 0 to 359.

heightFeet.description: The height above the ground under the point, in feet, held to 100 to 10000.

plane.description: The plane this world is flown in. Left out, it is flown in the trainer.

point.description: A point on the canvas, east and south of its middle, in world units.

row.description: One of the environment's own elements. Its label and its note are read off the element.

config.description: The element's ranges as the world draws them.

base.description: The ranges a gradient's shade is measured from.

shades.description: How far either end of each gradient is drawn from its base colour.

region.description: A region a placement covers: one of the kinds the builder draws - disc, ring, stroke, rect, ellipse, polygon, path - or two combined, or one set down moved, turned and stretched.

placement.description: Something the builder placed: an element, an erase batch, a runway template's group of members, or an object standing on the ground. A placement may carry more than the fields named here, which the builder adds as it needs to.

config.description: The element's ranges, each held to its bounds when the file is read, and the point it was dropped at. An object's are its point, its heading in degrees and its scale, held to 0.5 to 3.

prefab.description: An object's prefab, by its id: the catalogue entry it was placed from.

template.description: A group's template, by its id.

members.description: A group's members: placements of their own, never another group.

recipe.description: A building as parts of simple shapes, in metres in its own frame - x across, y up from the ground, z the way it faces - copied into an object when it is placed. Read whole or refused: a part out of its bounds is not guessed at.

solid.description: False for something the aircraft flies over rather than into, such as a park.

part.description: One part of a recipe - a box, a wedge (a roof's triangular prism), a cylinder or a cone - its base standing on the point it names.

at.description: Where the part's base stands, in metres: x, y and z.

turn.description: A turn about the part's upright, in degrees.

size.description: A box's or a wedge's width, height and depth, in metres.

ridge.description: Where a wedge's ridge runs: down its middle, or along its +x edge.

top.description: A cylinder's radius at its top, where it narrows.

segments.description: How many sides a cylinder or a cone is drawn with.
